correctness.rationale: Normalize by x=a+ht; normalized sixth derivatives contribute h^6 and the integral contributes h, giving h^7. Both reflected rules are exact on degrees 0–5, checked by substitution and independently in exact symbolic arithmetic. Using Taylor's integral remainder starting at 0, the order-six kernels are the corresponding error functionals on (x-s)_+^5/120. Substitution of the right endpoint jets yields K±=z²(±3√5/2−3−z)/720 with z=s(1−s). Their difference is √5 z²/240 and is strictly positive inside. The normalized error is a weighted average of 1/2−1/√5−z/(3√5). For any continuous nonzero nonnegative sixth derivative the ratio is strictly between the two endpoints; the closed interval stated in the proof is the closure of attainable ratios (as the proof and limitations specify elsewhere), not nonzero equality cases. Smooth derivative bumps recover the endpoints as limits, including one approaching an edge from inside, so the unique fixed-affine minimax choice is the midpoint with half-width 1/(24√5). The sign reversal and summation over a partition preserve the inequalities. Independent high-precision checks reproduce all stated exp(x) values and probe concentration at midpoint and edge using polynomial sixth derivatives: python3 /workspace/reproductions/check_frozen_math.py 2. These diagnostic runs do not replace the all-function kernel proof. Uploaded checker inspected but not executed.
